questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following oxides in correct order of their acidic character.
questions.solution:
Acidic character of oxides in group 15 to 18 elements decreases down the group. As we move down the group, the atomic size increases and electronegativity decreases. The oxide in the higher oxidation state of the elements is more acidic than that of lower oxidation state. In $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{I}), \mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (II) and $\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ (IV), N, $P$ and As are in +3 oxidation state respectively whereas in $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5$ (III) the $\mathrm{N}$ is in +5 oxidation state. So, the acidity order is

\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5>\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_3>\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{O}_3>\mathrm{As}_2 \mathrm{O}_3 \text {, i.e. } \mathrm{III}>\mathrm{I}>\mathrm{II}>\mathrm{IV}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following represents correct order of oxidising power of halogens with water?
questions.solution:
Whenever one of the halogens is involved in oxidising a species in solution, the halogen is reduced to a halide ion associated with water molecules. The following reactions illustrate this process ${ }^{\circ}\mathrm{F}_2(g)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{~F}^{-}(a q)\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{Cl}_2(g)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}(a q) \\ & \mathrm{Br}_2(l)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Br}^{-}(a q) \\ & \mathrm{I}_2(g)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{I}^{-}(a q)\end{aligned}$
Smaller the size of ion, higher is the energy released when the ion is hydrated. Since, the size of ions increases in the order $\mathrm{F}^{-} \lt  \mathrm{Cl}^{-} \lt  \mathrm{Br}^{-} \lt  \mathrm{I}^{-}$. The order of hydration energy is

\mathrm{F}^{-}(a q)>\mathrm{Cl}^{-}(a q)>\mathrm{Br}^{-}(a q)>\mathrm{I}^{-}(a q)

Because of very high hydration enthalpy of the fluoride ion, $\mathrm{F}_2$ gets very easily reduced followed by $\mathrm{Cl}_2$, then $\mathrm{Br}_2$ and $\mathrm{I}_2$. Therefore, the correct order of oxidising power of halogens is $\mathrm{F}_2\gt \mathrm{Cl}_2\gt \mathrm{Br}_2\gt \mathrm{I}_2$.

Oxygen shows $-2,-1,+1$ and +2 oxidation states.

\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~S} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Se} < \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{Te}

In Fischer Ringe's method, air free from moisture and $\mathrm{CO}_2$ is passed over a heated mixture $\left(800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ of $90 \%\mathrm{CaC}_2+10 \% \mathrm{CaCl}_2$ in an iron tube, when following reactions take place
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{CaC}_2+\mathrm{N}_2 \stackrel{800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CaCN}_2+\mathrm{C} \\
& 2 \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{O} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CO} \\
& \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{O}_2 \longrightarrow \mathrm{CO}_2 \\
& 2 \mathrm{CaC}_2+3 \mathrm{CO}_2 \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CaCO}_3+5 \mathrm{C} \\
& \mathrm{CuO}+\mathrm{CO} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}+\mathrm{CO}_2
\end{aligned}\mathrm{CO}_2$ gas is now absorbed by $\mathrm{KOH}$ solution.
Thus a mixture of inert gases is obtained.
